verdicts.why: Saying something again is reported flatly; any tedium in the sentences comes from the speaker, not the verb.
Doing something again is plain description with no attitude toward the doer.
An event recurring is stated without approval or disapproval.
Duration in time, as in 'at length', measures without judging.
A spatial dimension; there is no attitude in a measurement.
The abstract property of extent carries no side.
Going back somewhere is reported neutrally; the feeling attached in the sentences belongs to the characters.
A homecoming named plainly; the word does not warm or cool it.
Getting something back is a plain transaction with no judgement of anyone.
Information about events; the text has to add 'good' or 'dreadful' because the word itself takes no side.
Even for tittle-tattle spread at Meryton, 'news' is the plain neighbour that 'gossip' would judge against.
Reported information in print, named without attitude.
A spatial adverb; no attitude is possible toward a direction.
Coverage of an area is pure description.
Throughout a space; nothing is being judged.
Formal register is not connotation; 'in this way' says nothing about the speaker's attitude to what follows.
A logical connective that marks consequence and nothing more.
Moving toward a place is neutral; the sentences are only table-of-contents headings, but the sense itself judges nothing.
Being in charge is stated as a role, not praised or belittled by the verb.
Going in front of others is positional description without attitude.
Playing an instrument is named plainly; Elizabeth's reluctance is hers, not the word's.
Handling bracelets or toying with an idea is described, not disparaged; 'fiddle with' would be the loaded neighbour, this is the plain one.
Performing on an instrument takes no side on the performer or the music.
A temporal marker; nothing to approve or dismiss.
Rhythmic movement to music, named without any view of the dancers; the mortification in one sentence is the character's, not the noun's.
